title: Adding an unused tape preserves computation
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over an alphabet $\Gamma$ with no work tapes, and let $f\colon\Gamma^*\to\Gamma^*$ and $T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. If $M$ computes $f$ in time $T$, then the machine obtained by adding one unused work tape also computes $f$ in time $T$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$
replaced:
Let $M$ be a Turing machine over an alphabet $\Gamma$ with no work tapes that computes a
function $f$ on words over $\Gamma$ within time $T$, i.e.\ on every input $x$ the run of
$M$ has halted after $T(\abs{x})$ steps with output $f(x)$. Then the machine obtained
from $M$ by adding one unused work tape also computes $f$ within time $T$.
